title: Frag-seq
scope: Underwood 2010 FragSeq implementation, extracted from the Illumina Frag-seq schematic and the Frag-seq row of the poster. FragSeq/FRAG-Seq are source spellings of this target. The prepared starting boundary is purified nuclear RNA folded in vitro, corrected from the diagram’s polyA caption. Three independently routed preparations are retained: P1 digestion, untreated endogenous 5′P control, and PNK-treated endogenous-break control. The represented library contains 20-100 nucleotide, end-compatible RNA inserts copied to separate cDNA products. It probes in vitro RNA accessibility, with known nuclear ncRNAs as the demonstrated biological target. Neighboring PARTE and CapSeq poster rows and unrelated catalogue citations are outside scope. PCR/barcoding, pooling, SOLiD3 sequencing and cutting-score analysis are reported downstream in the paper, but are not added as operations beyond the diagram’s cDNA endpoints; the Illumina catalogue does not establish that the original experiment used an Illumina platform.

operations.label: Digest folded nuclear RNA with P1
operations.description: Limited endonuclease P1 digestion cleaves accessible single-stranded regions of the nuclear RNA, producing new RNA termini while leaving a mixed fragment preparation.
operations.mechanism: P1 cleaves the RNA phosphodiester backbone preferentially in single-stranded regions; a scission creates an upstream 3′OH and a downstream 5′ monophosphate. These are new ends on complementary products, not two isolated fractions.
operations.information_effect: Fragment boundaries encode P1-accessible positions in the in vitro RNA fold. Endogenous compatible ends can also enter this preparation, so the treatment is interpreted relative to the no-nuclease control.
